summary: Constellation answers the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners' request for clarification, opposing any use of the Point of Change in Ownership for co-located load and asking that eligibility terms for electrically proximate load not disqualify large loads.
ask: Deny the Transmission Owners' clarification request; if granted, make clear PJM and the owners must propose terms that encourage new transmission services and speedy large load interconnection.

points.point: Constellation says it responds only to the clarification request and calls the rehearing arguments premature.
points.quote: Exelon and FirstEnergy’s arguments are premature and barred by Rule 713 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure.

points.point: It calls the Point of Change in Ownership request a collateral attack on prior FERC rulings in the co-location dockets.
points.quote: This request for clarification is a thinly-veiled collateral attack on the Commission’s previous rulings in Docket Numbers ER26- 1088-000 and ER26-1479-000.

points.point: It asks FERC to clarify that eligibility requirements must not be so prescriptive that they disqualify large loads.
points.quote: any eligibility requirements PJM and the Transmission Owners propose in their initial filings must not be so prescriptive as to improperly disqualify large loads

points.point: It also asks that no reference point be used to define electrically proximate large load in a way that undermines speedy interconnection.
points.quote: may not use the Point of Change in Ownership, or any other point of reference, to define “electrically proximate large load” in a manner that likewise undermines speedy interconnection

throughLine.text: Answer to the Transmission Owners' E-7 clarification request on how large load and electrically proximate load are defined relative to the point of interconnection.
